name: Primary Laryngeal Lymphangioma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Laryngeal Lymphangioma

criteria.description: Presence of a painless, soft, cystic mass in the laryngeal region causing airway symptoms
MRI or CT demonstrating multiloculated cystic lesions consistent with lymphatic malformation in the larynx
Biopsy showing dilated lymphatic channels lined by endothelial cells without atypia
Exclusion of other cystic or neoplastic laryngeal lesions by clinical and imaging evaluation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (clinical presentation, imaging characteristics, and histopathology) must be met for definitive diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging and confirmed by histopathology.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multiloculated cystic mass in the larynx
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic soft, compressible swelling localized to the laryngeal area
searchTerms: multisection cystic mass in voice box

pathognomonic.notes: Due to mass effect within the larynx

common.notes: Voice changes caused by involvement of vocal cords
Inspiratory stridor from partial airway obstruction
Difficulty swallowing due to mass effect
External neck swelling may be present if lesion extends beyond larynx

occasional.notes: Rare bleeding from fragile lymphatic vessels

rare.notes: Life-threatening airway obstruction in severe cases

rare.symptomName: Infection or cellulitis of the lymphangioma

laboratory: Generally normal blood tests; inflammatory markers may be elevated if infected
imaging: MRI showing multiloculated, cystic, non-enhancing lesions in the larynx
CT scan demonstrating hypodense cystic masses without solid components
genetic: No known genetic mutations specifically associated with primary laryngeal lymphangioma
other: Histopathology confirming dilated lymphatic channels lined by flat endothelial cells

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of blood-filled vascular channels rather than lymphatic
More common in infants with cutaneous hemangiomas
Uniloculated cystic lesion without multiloculated appearance
No lymphatic endothelial lining on histology
Usually does not cause progressive airway obstruction

redFlags: Stridor at rest or respiratory distress
Sudden increase in lesion size with pain or bleeding
references: Smith RJH, et al. Vascular anomalies of the head and neck. Otolaryngol Clin North Am. 2018;51(1):1-14.
Orphanet Report Series: Primary Laryngeal Lymphangioma, ORPHA:137926.
